cards.Description: Urdu Muhavray and Kahawatein (Idioms and Proverbs)
cards.note: Debate: For Urdu speakers 'Urdu Words' never runs out, so no one ever fails. Muhavray (idioms) and kahawatein (proverbs) keep the card in Urdu, make it a real challenge and still have many well-known answers. The challenger's amended English gloss matches both terms.
Debate: Overlaps the live 'Pakistani Public Holidays' card (the Eids, 14 August, Milad). Once those are taken, only a handful of well-known answers are left.
too narrow (5 prayers); overlaps Types of Salah

clearer; Debate: 'Animals Found in Pakistan' nearly duplicates Animals (4). Limiting it to wild animals gives it its own answers: markhor, snow leopard, Indus dolphin, ibex, urial, chinkara, bears, jackal, mugger crocodile.
wording; Debate: Most people know only a handful of dams. Adding the real Indus barrages (Sukkur, Kotri, Guddu, Taunsa, Chashma, Jinnah, Panjnad) gives enough answers to play.
designers too narrow/celebrity; brands widely known
few known Pakistani perfume brands; reframed
merged into Pakistani Apps and Websites

cards.note: New card (debate): Accurate, with many well-known answers (Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, Khaibar, Hunain, Yarmouk, Qadisiyyah, Hattin, Ain Jalut). Nothing like it is in the deck.

cards.Description: Occasions When We Say a Dua
cards.note: New card (debate): An everyday Islamic theme with many answers (eating, sleeping, travelling, leaving home, entering the masjid, after wudu). It is different from Good Deeds and Sunnah Habits.
New card (debate): Has about 10 well-known Pakistani answers (gajar, suji, besan, sohan, anday, badam, kaddu, chanay ki daal, habshi). It is not a duplicate of Mithai or Desserts.
New card (debate): A broad, easy card with many answers (pakoray, samosay, jalebi, puri, kachori, fries, fried fish, nimko). It is not a duplicate.
New card (debate): Relatable desi humour. It asks for items, not actions, so it does not duplicate 'Things You Do When Mehmaan Are Coming'.
New card (debate): Funny and relatable, with many answers (ice cream tubs, biscuit tins as sewing boxes, shopping bags, jam jars, old shirts as pochay). Nothing like it is in the deck.

cards.Description: Rooms and Parts of a House
cards.note: New card (debate): Has many answers (sehan, chhat, verandah, drawing room, store, garage, balcony, staircase). The existing room cards ask for objects, not rooms.
New card (debate): The colour series has Green, Yellow, Red, White, Black, Blue and Brown but no Orange. Easy answers: kinnow, carrot, papaya, jalebi, marigold, Fanta, tiger.
New card (debate): A new property card with plenty of local answers (gas cylinder, deg, almirah, fridge, sack of wheat, truck). Not in the deck.

New card (debate): The challenger's version of P7. Leaving out animals stops it from turning into the Animals card and keeps the household-object spirit of the With Buttons/Handles/Holes cards: charpai, chair, table, stool, takht, ironing stand, tripod, peerhi.
New card (debate): A household-object card with a local feel (pateela, pressure cooker, tiffin, deg, kettle, achaar jar, thermos). Different from Things You Can Fill With Water.
New card (debate): An easy, funny property card (gold, mirror, bangles, steel utensils, coins, new Eid shoes, a bald head). Not in the deck.

cards.Description: Restaurants and Food Chains in Pakistan
cards.note: New card (debate): The challenger's version of P10. It gives players in every city answers (KFC, McDonald's, Savour Foods, Student Biryani, OPTP, Broadway, Cheezious, Kababjees, Bundu Khan) and drops Monal Islamabad, which was demolished in 2024. Different from Fast Food Items and Pakistani Brands.
